title: Motors & Movement Arcade
intro: Six rounds on motors, H-bridges and differential drive. Get them right first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: What creates the magnetic field that makes a motor's coil spin?
rounds.explain: Current through a wire always creates a magnetic field — that's the physics fact the whole motor is built on.

rounds.prompt: A motor is under too much load for its current voltage. What actually happens?
options: It slows down smoothly and safely
It stalls — RPM drops to zero and current spikes upward
rounds.explain: A stalled motor keeps trying to draw current with nothing spinning to regulate it, so current climbs instead of producing motion.

rounds.prompt: Match each H-bridge switch combination to what it does.
rounds.explain: Diagonal pairs drive the motor one way or the other. Same-side pairs short the battery — a real driver chip makes that impossible.

rounds.prompt: Why can't a controller GPIO pin power a motor directly?
options: GPIO pins can only supply a small current, far less than a motor needs
GPIO pins are too fast for motors
rounds.explain: A pin's ~40mA is nowhere near a motor's ~800mA demand — a driver chip bridges that gap.

rounds.prompt: ARIA's wheel is 6.5cm in diameter. What does one full wheel rotation give you?
options: A distance equal to the wheel's circumference, about 20cm
A distance equal to the wheel's diameter
It depends on the motor's voltage
rounds.explain: Distance per rotation is always circumference (π × diameter) — a purely geometric fact about the wheel.

rounds.prompt: Left wheel at +50, right wheel at −50. What does ARIA do?
rounds.explain: Equal, opposite wheel speeds cancel forward motion and produce pure rotation — the signature differential-drive spin.
